name: South Asia
blurb: From Himalayan ice to the Sundarbans mangroves: a crowded region where rivers, tigers, elephants and vultures share space with nearly 1.7 billion people.

issues.title: The Vulture Crisis

drivers.name: Other veterinary drugs that harm vultures
Loss of safe feeding and nesting sites

fact.text: Three Gyps vulture species endemic to South Asia have declined by more than 98% in the Indian subcontinent since the early 1990s, and the veterinary drug diclofenac has been shown to be the major cause of the collapse.
fact.source: Bird Conservation International 21(1), 72–75 (2011), “Diclofenac is toxic to the Himalayan Vulture”

issues.realWorld: Never give pets or livestock medicines that are harmful to wildlife, return unused medicines to a pharmacy take-back scheme, and support vulture conservation groups.

issues.title: The Ganga’s Sewage

drivers.name: Sewage from towns along the river

fact.text: India’s Ministry of Jal Shakti told Parliament in March 2026, citing the Central Pollution Control Board, that the Ganga’s faecal coliform bathing criterion is met along the whole river in Uttarakhand and Jharkhand but only in certain stretches of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal, where polluted stretches of the main stem remain.
fact.source: Ministry of Jal Shakti, Rajya Sabha reply on the status of the Namami Gange Programme (PIB, 23 March 2026), citing CPCB

issues.realWorld: Never pour oil, paint or chemicals down a drain, support river clean-up groups, and ask your local authority how your sewage is treated.

issues.title: The Sinking Mangroves

fact.text: A 2019 study projected that, under climate change and sea-level rise, there will be no suitable Bengal tiger habitat remaining in the Bangladesh Sundarbans by 2070.
fact.source: Mukul et al., Science of the Total Environment 663, 830–840 (2019)

issues.realWorld: Ask where prawns and shrimp come from and prefer mangrove-friendly certified or locally farmed seafood, and support mangrove-planting and community-protection groups.

issues.title: Himalayan Water Towers

drivers.name: Floods and landslides as glaciers melt

fact.text: ICIMOD’s 2023 assessment found that glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya disappeared 65% faster in the 2010s than in the previous decade, and that on current emissions pathways they could lose up to 80% of their current volume by 2100.
fact.source: ICIMOD, Water, Ice, Society, and Ecosystems in the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HI-WISE) report (2023)

also.source: Down To Earth (19 June 2023), on the ICIMOD report

issues.realWorld: Cut your own emissions where you can, and support early-warning systems and community adaptation work in mountain valleys.

issues.title: The Smoke Season
sites: A wetland at the edge of the fields

fact.text: A 2025 study in npj Climate and Atmospheric Science found that crop-residue burning in Punjab contributed only about 14% of the PM2.5 over Delhi-NCR in October–November 2022, and named road traffic and construction among the other major sources.
fact.source: Mangaraj et al., npj Climate and Atmospheric Science (2025), “Weak coupling of observed surface PM2.5 in Delhi-NCR with rice crop residue burning in Punjab and Haryana”

issues.realWorld: Never burn rubbish or garden waste, choose lower-emission transport where you can, and support farmers’ schemes that use crop residue instead of burning it.

issues.title: Red Gold Smugglers

fact.text: A TRAFFIC and WWF-India factsheet (January 2023) found that, in CITES trade records for 2016–2020, India reported exporting more than 19,049 tonnes of red sanders logs while importing countries reported only about 4,610 tonnes, a discrepancy in the reporting of the trade.
fact.source: TRAFFIC and WWF-India, Factsheet on India’s Red Sanders in Illegal Wildlife Trade (January 2023)

issues.realWorld: Do not buy red sandalwood products, check that any rare-wood item comes with CITES paperwork, and support anti-trafficking groups such as TRAFFIC.

issues.title: Elephants and the Railway

drivers.name: Roads, railways and mines across corridors

fact.text: India’s DNA-based elephant survey for 2021–25, published by the Wildlife Institute of India in 2025, estimated 22,446 wild Asian elephants (confidence interval 18,255–26,645); the report says the figure is not comparable with past counts and should be treated as a new baseline.
fact.source: Wildlife Institute of India, Status of Elephants in India: DNA based Synchronous All India population estimation of elephants (SAIEE) 2021–2025

also.source: Down To Earth (15 October 2025), on the census release

issues.realWorld: Support groups that secure elephant corridors and fund safe crossings, and choose responsibly sourced sand, stone and building materials where you can.
